- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–3% for the next 3–7 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise; cap forecast at +10% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to reverse trend; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates downside risk in bearish sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for days 15–30 if sentiment <0.4.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, model often lags; add 0.2–0.5% to forecast for next 2–3 days to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending downward, model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
